newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka, Tamil Tiger rebels in war of words.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka, Tamil Tiger rebels in war of words.

text.p: Sri Lanka and Tamil Tiger rebels were locked in a war of words on Tuesday with each blaming the other for a bomb explosion in government-held Vavuniya town that killed two people.

A bomb attached to a bicycle exploded on Monday in a marketplace in Vavuniya, some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo, wounding 26 people, mostly civilians. Two of them later died in hospital.
The blast followed a daring raid by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels at the military's forward positions near Vavuniya last week.
Police officials in largely Tamil dominated Vavuniya said on Monday that the bomb was the handiwork of the rebels.
But the LTTE accused the government of triggering the blast to discredit them.
They said in a statement that the government was making up stories to deflect attention from its "worsening military predicament".
"Any clear thinking person would appreciate the sheer absurdity of the LTTE engaging in activity of this kind against Tamils in Vavuniya," the statement said.
"The ability of a recognised government to undertake such callous acts against Tamil civilians for the purpose of propaganda reveals quite unequivocally its true colours," it said.

The LTTE are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.

The war of words has intensified in recent days since some 20,000 troops launched Operation Jaya Sikuru (Sure of Victory) against the LTTE through the northern brush jungles of the Wanni to open a key highway linking Vavuniya to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.
Troops backed by tanks, artillery and air cover have captured key rebel towns in the Wanni.

But the rebels struck back last week, hitting at the rear of the troops and breaching military defences just north of Vavuniya. A military ammunition dump was blown up in fierce fighting, affecting the main operation.
On Monday, the government blasted a separatist claim that food supplies to the rebel heartland of Wanni had been stopped.

"The government of Sri Lanka wishes to categorically state that there has been no change in the government's long followed policy of sending all essential supplies required by the people in the uncleared areas," the foreign ministry said in a statement.
The LTTE said at the weekend that food convoys to the Wanni region had been stopped by the military.
The ministry statement said the rebels were trying to divert attention from the reversals they were facing in the on-going operation.

The LTTE have regularly accused Colombo of killing Tamil civilians and destroying crops and property under the pretext of opening a supply route to Jaffna, and of continuing a food siege of the Wanni.

But the ministry statement claimed Sri Lanka had not used food as a weapon and had continued to supply essential items to the rebel-held areas in spite of the knowledge that "a bulk of these supplies are commandeered by the LTTE for their sustenance".
The LTTE has denied the charge.
